external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers for field dispatch.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the console and schedule importer for dispatch operations.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process that pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, parses XML, archives documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or the session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store containing each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: The duty engineer loads the console from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser. ... our corporate web host serves it.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: The duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. The allowed origins and whether credentials are allowed were not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens a WebSocket to receive live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull SOAP feed
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS every hour.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer, or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: It presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The boundary of the other company that publishes planned work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is confidential because it contains crew names, crew mobile numbers, and tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database holds crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
